questions.q: What real cloud-provider ceiling did classic notification mode run into at scale?
options: Each stream needed its own dedicated queue/subscription, capped at 100 streams per container on AWS/GCP and 500 on Azure
Classic notifications had no limit at all, which is why File Events was never needed
Classic notifications could only run on AWS, never Azure or GCP
Directory listing mode had the ceiling, not classic notifications
questions.explain: Since each Auto Loader stream with classic notifications required its own dedicated queue/subscription, cloud providers' caps on notification resources per container became a hard ceiling: 100 on AWS/GCP, 500 on Azure.

questions.q: What architectural change does File Events make to avoid that ceiling?
options: A single, Databricks-managed queue/subscription per external location, shared by many Auto Loader streams instead of one queue per stream
It removes queues entirely and uses pure directory listing under the hood
It requires each stream to request its own separate cloud account
It eliminates the need for any cloud storage at all
questions.explain: File Events sets up one queue/subscription per external location rather than per stream, so many streams can share it — directly avoiding the per-container notification resource cap.

questions.q: What option turns on managed File Events in an Auto Loader stream or a Declarative Pipeline's cloud_files() call?
options: cloudFiles.useManagedFileEvents set to True
cloudFiles.backfillInterval set to 0
cloudFiles.format set to 'events'
spark.conf.set only, with no stream-level option available
questions.explain: cloudFiles.useManagedFileEvents (True) is the option that enables File Events, usable both in a plain Auto Loader stream and inside a Declarative Pipeline's cloud_files() call.

questions.q: What happens to cloudFiles.backfillInterval once managed File Events is enabled?
options: It is ignored, since the periodic re-check it used to control is now handled automatically by the managed service
It becomes mandatory and must be set to a non-zero value
It is renamed to cloudFiles.fileEventsInterval with identical behavior
It now controls how often the cloud queue itself is deleted and recreated
questions.explain: Because the managed file events service already handles periodic re-listing to ensure no files are missed, the old backfillInterval setting is simply ignored under File Events.

questions.q: How does File Events change the limits on Databricks Job file arrival triggers?
options: It removes both the 10,000-file directory cap and the 50-trigger-per-workspace cap, making both unlimited
It has no effect on file arrival triggers at all
It reduces the file arrival trigger limit to 1,000 files, stricter than before
File arrival triggers are deprecated entirely once File Events is enabled
questions.explain: Without File Events, file arrival triggers rely on directory listing and are capped at 10,000 files per directory and 50 triggers per workspace; with File Events enabled, both become unlimited.
